relations.subject: tool:couchbase-cli-setting-password-policy
relations.evidence: Allows retrieval of the current password policy and creating a new password policy for new Couchbase users. This allows administrators to customize the complexity of user passwords.

notable_absence.finding: No role:/privilege: concept is cited for who may --get or --set the password policy - only the shared generic 'unauthorized error' boilerplate. Password-complexity policy is a security-relevant, cluster-wide setting comparable in kind to setting-security.md's TLS settings, yet like that page it names no role at all.

cross_component_finding: The page has THREE independent flag-name mismatches between its own SYNOPSIS/OPTIONS/EXAMPLES sections, all on the same small option surface: (1) SYNOPSIS declares `--special-chars` but OPTIONS defines `--special-char` (no 's'); (2) SYNOPSIS and OPTIONS both say `--digit` but the EXAMPLES section's own worked command uses `--digits 1` (plural, never defined anywhere else on the page); (3) OPTIONS lists `--uppercase`, `--lowercase`, `--digit`, `--special-char` in that order but the SYNOPSIS's own bracket list and the EXAMPLES prose ('contain an upper case letter, lower case letter, and a digit') each enumerate a different subset. A reader constructing a command purely from this page's own EXAMPLES would pass an option (`--digits`) that OPTIONS never documents. This is the densest concentration of synopsis/options/examples drift found in the batch on a single short page - strong, cumulative evidence for the round's lighter-TW-review hypothesis.
cross_product_finding: n/a - no Capella/Mobile/SDK content; password complexity policy via couchbase-cli is a Server-only local-user setting.
